decisions.reason: Resizing the main board to 70×50 does not change the established three-board architecture or the roles and exclusions of its boards.
The requested resize and rough rearrangement do not alter the existing top-edge, alignment, cable-routing, or accessibility placement constraints.
The 70×50 dimension applies to the main board and does not change the power board's mechanical form factor.
The source separately confirms that the ESP32 may remain at the edge, and that requirement is already represented by a same-message Event; the board resize requires no additional change.
Changing the board outline does not alter which ESP32 pins require breakout holes or the existing freedom to place those holes anywhere.
The statement about routing the resized main board on four layers does not modify the power board's established four-layer stack.
The client rejects combining connectors and retains separate JST connections, which is consistent with the candidate's existing separate power-and-signal connector state rather than a change to it.
The main-board resize does not change the reset connector, panel mounting, or EN-to-GND behavior.
Retaining separate JST connectors is compatible with the existing interboard power connector, topology, and pin-order rules and does not change them.
The main-board dimensions and connector-layout preference do not change the charge-status indication path or its connector and resistor requirements.
The main-board outline change has no necessary effect on DCDC1 voltage regulation or Schottky-drop compensation.
The resize does not alter the panel power-button connector, its main-board location, or its connection to PWRON.
